data.summary: Voltage log over 46.9 h (84433 samples, one every 2 s; voltage series m_31acd1a5c9aa and clock m_8a271b557718 keep one per minute). Protocol: cycle 1 charge at 2 mA/cm2: 0.00-13.90 h; cycle 1 relax after charge at 0 mA/cm2: 13.90-16.90 h; cycle 1 discharge at 2 mA/cm2: 16.90-26.20 h; cycle 1 relax after discharge at 0 mA/cm2: 26.20-29.20 h; cycle 2 charge at 4 mA/cm2: 29.20-36.18 h; cycle 2 relax after charge at 0 mA/cm2: 36.18-39.18 h; cycle 2 discharge at 4 mA/cm2: 39.18-43.91 h; cycle 2 relax after discharge at 0 mA/cm2: 43.91-46.91 h. Plating markers (time into each charge): cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage first goes below 0 V vs Li/Li+ after 7.43 h +/-0.68 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -0.0 mV logged) — m_f2b2903ae64e; cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage first comes within 5 mV of the final-hour median (-0.04681 V) and stays in that band for at least 30 min (an operational plateau definition) after 10.21 h +/-10.21 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -41.8 mV logged) — m_c0d5200b4e1f; cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage reaches its lowest value in this charge after 11.44 h +/-2.46 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -51.8 mV logged) — m_a3e03d8590b9; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage first goes below 0 V vs Li/Li+ after 0.22 h +/-0.03 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -0.0 mV logged) — m_80cd783112ae; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage first comes within 5 mV of the final-hour median (-0.04634 V) and stays in that band for at least 30 min (an operational plateau definition) after 4.87 h +/-4.87 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -51.3 mV logged) — m_9f99a4d3ec5b; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage reaches its lowest value in this charge after 0.81 h +/-0.42 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -102.9 mV logged) — m_7cb280545dcb. The stated 10 h onset can't be reconciled under the assumptions that onset = first 0 V crossing and voltage error is within +/-10 mV: its time window still lies before 9.5 h. The logged 5 mV plateau is an operational definition, with no precise physical onset established at this voltage accuracy. Cycle 2 is in the log, not in this movie. The full source log is retained for computation; the returned series keeps one sample per minute.

data.answer: No pale lithium plating was visible at about 10.2 hours on the movie clock (claim_f781c4f289), and pale plating was first clearly visible at about 11.5 hours (claim_131fd8584b), so visible plating starts sometime between those times, after 10 hours of charging. The voltage log first fell below zero much earlier, at about 7.4 hours during the first charge (claim_ec5e84b361), a difference of about 4 hours from the first clear video plating. Under the assumption that falling below zero marks the start of plating, the voltage-log time and the stated onset after 10 hours cannot be reconciled; the voltage drop by itself does not prove that plating had started at that earlier time.
data.not_proven: The exact moment plating began between about 10.2 and 11.5 hours is not proven, because the movie clock is coarse and plating could have been present but too faint to see in the earlier frames.

lessons.text: Filament length measured from the right electrode can include growth within or along the electrode edge, so tip position relative to both electrodes should be checked directly before claiming a filament bridged the gap.

Lithium plating in this cross-section appears as a pale fringe on the separator-facing graphite surface, so onset should be bracketed between the last clean frame and the first fringed frame rather than timed from a single frame.

lessons.text: The movie clock bound of about twenty minutes is too coarse to prove a precise plating onset or growth speed, so video timing should be compared to the voltage log only within that bound.
